verses.english: This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

verses.pali: “Te, bhikkhave, sattā suparihīnā ye ariyāya paññāya parihīnā.
verses.english: “Those sentient beings are truly bereft, mendicants, who are bereft of noble wisdom.

verses.pali: Te diṭṭheva dhamme dukkhaṁ viharanti savighātaṁ saupāyāsaṁ sapariḷāhaṁ;
verses.english: They live unhappily in this very life—with distress, anguish, and fever—

verses.pali: kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā duggati pāṭikaṅkhā.
verses.english: and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a bad rebirth.

verses.pali: Te, bhikkhave, sattā aparihīnā ye ariyāya paññāya aparihīnā.
verses.english: Those sentient beings are not bereft who are not bereft of noble wisdom.

verses.pali: Te diṭṭheva dhamme sukhaṁ viharanti avighātaṁ anupāyāsaṁ apariḷāhaṁ;
verses.english: In this very life they’re happy—free of distress, anguish, and fever—

verses.pali: kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugati pāṭikaṅkhā”ti.
verses.english: and when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect a good rebirth.”
Wisdom is best in the world,
the ending of rebirth and continued existence.

verses.pali: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
verses.english: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
